sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Nevertheless, this is included in lower awe, because his contemplation is of Elokus relative to the worlds, so even when contemplating being like a silent stone, the sublimity of Ein Sof beyond worlds is not felt as much.

translations.translation: However, nevertheless this is included in lower awe,
for the main focus of his contemplation is upon Elokus as it relates to the worlds,
and therefore,
even when he contemplates that he is merely in the category of a silent stone,
there is not felt within him
(so much)
the sublimity of Ein Sof that is above the worlds, before Whom everything is considered as nothing.
And from this it is understood,
that this [matter] that supernal awe is from the sublimity of Ein Sof that is above the worlds,
the intention in this is that this very concept is felt by him.
And based on this, one must understand further regarding that which concerning Tzion
(supernal awe)
the term Elokim is stated.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason "Praise your Elokim, O Tzion" is because He strengthened the bars of your gates, referring to the gevurot of the name Elokim that limit the flow from the Ohr Ein Sof, which is above differentiation, so that external forces cannot draw sustenance.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the maamar beginning "Shivchi" mentioned above,
that the reason for the statement "Praise your Elokim, O Tzion" is explained by the verse itself
(in the following verse)
"For He has strengthened the bars of your gates, etc."
And the concept is, as it is stated in the Mishnah,
"They compel him
(a resident of the city)
to build for the city a wall, doors, and a bar."
For a wall is to protect from the enemy, so that he does not enter the city,
and in order that the city's inhabitants may go out and come in,
they make an opening and a door in the wall,
and they make bars for the door,
so that only those who are fit to enter may enter the city.
And correspondingly, above,
the concept of the bars is the gevurot of the name Elokim, which limit the flow,
so that sustenance should not be drawn from it to the external forces.
And this is "Praise your Elokim, O Tzion"
(and the reason that the name Elokim is stated here is)
"For He has strengthened the bars of your gates,"
for in Tzion there is the drawing down of Ohr Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent
(as mentioned above),
for regarding this light, all are equal,
and therefore the gevurot of the name Elokim are needed to limit the flow that is drawn from this light,
so that the external forces should not draw sustenance.
And analogous to the statement "And to say to Tzion, 'You are My people,'"
that the flow from the aspect of Tzion will be only to "My people,"
to Israel.
And this is what the verse continues: "Bless your children within you,"
that the blessing and flow will be only to your children,
to Israel.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This is accomplished through the service of "judges and officers" in all your gates, refining the seven emotional attributes to be solely for Hashem, thereby creating the bars that prevent the flow from reaching the external forces.

translations.translation: And the maamar continues,
that this concept is accomplished through the service of "Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates."
"Your gates" are the fifty gates of Binah that are drawn from the intellect of Binah to the emotions of the heart.
And through the service of "Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates,"
that all seven emotional attributes
[each of which includes seven]
will be for Hashem alone,
through this, "the bars of your gates" are made,
so that the flow will not be drawn to the external forces, but only to Israel.
